body.p: Status of the Claims
The Office Action addresses and rejects claims 1, 4-5, 7-10, 13-14, and 16-18 Reconsideration is respectfully requested.
Claims 7 and 16 are canceled without prejudice or disclaimer.

Claims 1, 4-5, 8, 10, 13-14, and 17 are amended as indicated above. Support for these amendments can be found throughout the specification and drawings, for example, at least in original claims 7 and 16 and in FIG. 7 and paragraphs [0053]-[0059] of the published application. No new matter is added.

The Office Action rejects claims 1, 4-5, 7-10, 13-14, and 16-20 under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly being unpatentable over U.S. 2020/0130609 to Ibitoye ("Ibitoye") in view of U.S. 2022/0417359 to Tokuyama ("Tokuyama"), and U.S. 2011/0215900 to Corradino et al. ("Corradino"), and U.S. 2016/0046300 to Wingfield. ("Wingfield"). Office Action, pp. 5-11.
Applicants respectfully disagree. However, solely in order to advance prosecution, claim 1 is amended to recite, in part,
"a portable device and a vehicle terminal, each including a processor,
wherein first user information and second user information are input into the
portable device and the vehicle terminal;...
wherein the portable device and the vehicle terminal are further configured
to transmit the second user information to the server after being informed that the
new data set is stored in the server; and
wherein the second user information includes vehicle setting value linked
attribute information that only includes the Key IDs."
For example, with reference to FIG. 7 of the instant application, operation S120 transmits user information (e.g., vehicle setting values and attribute information linked with vehicle setting

values and includes a vehicle setting function and a Key ID matching with the vehicle setting function) to a server when the user information is input. In operations Si170-S 190, when the number of times unrecognizable user information received exceeds a predetermined number of times, the server stores the unrecognizable user information as a new data set and transmits this user information to the vehicle terminal and the portable device. Instant Specification, [0053]-[0056].

In operation S220, after the new data set is stored, the user information is received again. The input user information is the vehicle setting value linked with the attribute information, where only a Key ID is included. Instant Specification, [0057].

In operation S 180, the vehicle setting function matching with the Key ID Is already stored in the server. Therefore, in operation S220, even when inputting the vehicle setting value linked with the attribute information in which only the Key ID is included, instead of inputting the same user information of operation S 110, the server is capable of recognizing by linking the vehicle setting value received through operation S230 (the vehicle setting value input in operation S220) with the vehicle setting function. Instant Specification, [0058].

In contrast, Ibitoye merely discusses that an automated bumper protection roll updates a user device on a dashboard based on user input. Corradino merely discusses using a fingerprint scan as an attribute to identify a user when the fingerprint scan received to identify the user matches with a fingerprint scan as a key representing a setting selected by an account owner. Accordingly, Ibitoye and Corradino fail to teach or suggest "wherein the portable device and the vehicle terminal are further configured to transmit the second user information to the server after being informed that the new data set is stored in the server; and wherein the second user information includes vehicle setting value linked attribute information that only includes the Key IDs," as recited in amended claim 1. Tokuyama and Wingfield are relied upon for other claim features and fail to remedy these deficiencies.
For at least these reasons, claims 1 and 10 distingiush over Ibitoye, Tokuyama, Corradino, and Wingfield, alone or in any combination, and represent allowable subject matter. Claims 4-5,

8-10, 13-14, and 17-18 variously depend from claims 1 and 10 and also represent allowable subject matter at least due to their dependency from a patent-eligible claim. Claims 7 and 16 are canceled hereiwth and, therefore, the rejection of these claims is moot.

In conclusion, Applicants submit that all pending claims are in condition for allowance for at least the reasons discussed above, and allowance thereof is respectfully requested. Applicants' amendment of the claims does not constitute a concession that the claims are not allowable in their unamended form. The Examiner is encouraged to telephone the undersigned Agent for Applicants if such communication is deemed to expedite prosecution of this application.

No extension of time is believed to be due with this submission. However, in the event that a petition for extension of time is required to be submitted at this time, Applicants hereby petition under 37 C.F.R. § 1.136(a) for an extension of time for as many months as are required to ensure that the above-identified application does not become abandoned.

No fees are believed to be due in connection with this submission. However, if necessary, the Director is hereby authorized to charge any deficiency in the fees filed with this paper, asserted to be filed with this paper, or which should have been filed with this paper, to our Deposit Account No. 50-1943, under Order No. 347836.00101.
